newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian govt approves social security savings.
newsitem.headline: Belgian govt approves social security savings.

text.p: The Belgian government approved a series of temporary measures on Friday to save 10 billion Belgian francs ($0.3 billion) on its medical insurance spending.

Social affairs minister Magda De Galan told a news conference after the weekly cabinet meeting the measures, which involved among other things blocking or reducing fees paid to doctors and paramedics, would last six months.
After then the government hopes to put more structural changes in place to reduce social security spending.
In its 1997 budget unveiled in October the Belgian government promised 23 billion Belgian francs of savings in the social security sector as part of an overall 80-billion-franc austerity package.
With its sights on joining a futures European single currency, the government worked out a 1997 budget which aimed to cut the public deficit to 2.9 percent of GDP in 1997 .
